page: Microsoft Azure E8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processors operating at up to 3.525 GHz, this instance provisions 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of shared L3 cache, and 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 137 GB solid-state drive, and the instance operates without dedicated GPU acceleration under Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded processor capabilities, with stress-ng single-core throughput placing in the top quartile. Memory subsystem evaluations also yield strong marks, supported by a PassMark memory score of 2777.21 and memory read bandwidth reaching 515.37 GB/s in small-block cached environments. Conversely, heavily threaded decompression tasks like bzip3 and larger model inference show average to lower-tier results. Multi-core compute performance, Redis throughput reaching 8.2 million SET operations per second, and PassMark database operations remain consistently within the median range.

The 8:1 memory ratio provides favorable resource density for working sets that exceed typical general-purpose boundaries, minimizing paging overhead without paying for unnecessary compute units. Because local storage is limited to a modest 137 GB SSD, applications requiring extensive persistent data storage depend on attached remote premium block storage.

The E8as_v4 is technically tailored for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Primary workload fits include medium-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data mining pipelines, and business intelligence applications that benefit from high memory allocation alongside reliable single-thread compute.
description: Microsoft Azure E8as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores at 3.525 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM to deliver an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes 137 GB of temporary SSD storage, 32 MB of L3 cache, and no GPU accelerators. Synthetic and system benchmarks show strong memory subsystem ratings and high single-core compute performance, alongside standard throughput for Redis caching and relational database operations. While multi-threaded compression and large model processing show moderate efficiency, its generous memory capacity offers balanced resource density for memory-bound applications. The E8as_v4 is particularly suited for in-memory caches, intermediate-scale databases, and memory-heavy web services.
